title: The fly's ear-to-song circuit
description: Auditory Johnston's organ neurons, the wing and haltere sensory neurons that feed the song circuit, their strongest downstream auditory partners, male courtship-song neurons and wing motor neurons, and the strongest premotor inputs to that song circuit, with predicted neurotransmitters.

source.citation: Berg, S., Beckett, I. R., Costa, M., Schlegel, P., Januszewski, M., et al. (2025). Sexual dimorphism in the complete connectome of the Drosophila male central nervous system. bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.10.09.680999

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.attribution: Connectome and neurotransmitter predictions from MaleCNS male-cns:v1.0 by FlyEM (HHMI Janelia), the University of Cambridge, the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, and Google Research, licensed CC BY 4.0. Filtered to an ear-to-song subcircuit.

rules: Ear: every neuron typed JO-A or JO-B (sound-sensitive Johnston's organ subgroups).
Wing sense: the 150 nerve-cord sensory neurons sending the most synapses onto the song set (wing campaniform sensilla and haltere afferents).
Auditory: the 300 neurons receiving the most synapses from the ear, then the 300 receiving the most from ear plus that first hop.
Song: male courtship-song and wing-song types (pC1, pIP10, vPR6, vPR9, dPR1, TN1, vMS, dMS, aSP, vpoEN/IN, pMP2, DNp13, CL062) and the direct wing motor neurons.
Premotor: the 300 neurons sending the most synapses to the song set, then the 250 sending the most to song plus that hop.
Connections keep the whole-CNS threshold of at least 3 synapses among selected neurons, with original counts.

Transmitters use upstream consensus_nt predictions; the model maps acetylcholine to excitation, GABA, glutamate, and histamine to inhibition, and monoamines to weak excitation. Unknown transmitters are treated as excitatory.
